title: Prescriptions Controlled and Non-Controlled Partial Fill Terms
content:
A fill of Kestrel Prescriptions may be dispensed short of the prescribed quantity, with the balance owed to the patient, on the terms the handling class sets below: whether a short fill is allowed, how many calendar days the owed balance has to be completed, which date that window counts from, and how many owed balances may be open at the same time on one prescription.

| Handling class | Short fill with balance owed allowed | Completion window (calendar days) | Window counts from | Most owed balances open at once on one prescription |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | Yes | 14 | the date of the short fill | 1 |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | Yes | 14 | the date of the short fill | 1 |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | Yes | 14 | the date of the short fill | 1 |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | Yes | 14 | the date of the short fill | 1 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | Yes | 30 | the date the prescriber wrote the prescription | 1 |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | Yes | 7 | the date of the short fill | 1 |

The completion window is counted in calendar days from the anchor date named in the "window counts from" column, the anchor date being day 0.

## Worked readings (hypothetical dates)

- A Schedule II Controlled Prescription written on day 0 and dispensed short on day 5 has its window counted from the written date: day 30 after the written date is the last day of the window, whatever the date of the short fill.
- A Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription dispensed short on day 0 has a window whose last day is day 7 after the short fill.
- A Non-Controlled Acute Prescription dispensed short on day 0 has a window whose last day is day 14 after the short fill.
- On every class at most 1 owed balance may be open at the same time on one prescription.
